A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the stomata of tall trees do not have the capacity for tight control of transpiration rate, and the hydraulic feedback loop may not always be sufficient to maintain constant leaf turgor.
the hydraulic feedback loop is the primary mechanism by which stomata control leaf water potential and transpirational rate in tall trees.
the hydraulic feedback loop can be used to maintain constant leaf and guard cell water potential, but the ability to maintain constant guard cell turgor pressure is limited.

the hydraulic feedback loop is the primary mechanism by which stomata respond to water stress.
